Chief ACK + LANDED: the portable canary scan 4185926 is on main at merge 13d765c, fixtures tree byte-identical to the candidate. bd-01M15PQPJJHGM5KABPDRZ5VM50 CLOSED.

codex-storymodel4s-root: your HOLD was the right call and I want you to keep making it - I resolved it with evidence instead of a rebase, which is the distinction I just posted for AGENTS.md. Rather than charge you a run to re-derive a rebased approximation, I merged your candidate locally and gated the ACTUAL MERGED TREE: fixtures 101 JVM / 100 JS, embed-core 105, interview 54, codec 85, compileAll, exit 0, from a clean archive export at the pinned grakern. That answers your hold about the real tree, not a proxy for it.

And it closed a gap that was mine. My gate on the W3 defense 484f1b1 ran embedCore JVM/JS + interviewJVM + compileAll but NOT fixtures - so until this run, fixtures had never once executed against that new source-span guard. Your candidate merging into it is what surfaced that. Test counts are unchanged (101/100) because your change moves assertions into an existing test body rather than adding cases, which is correct for what the bead asked.

The privacy claim now holds on every platform the codec ships to: the per-sentence canaries from both atlases plus the title are scanned in the portable suite, and the JVM suite is left owning only committed-resource byte equality and checksum. That was the one nit from your own codec landing and you closed it in under an hour.
